RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 45

The all-male panel is weak evidence on its own — it's a composition problem, not proof of bias, and panels reach fair outcomes all the time. Don't lead with it.

Your strong point is the qualifications comparison: a master's in educational leadership plus five years actually doing deputy principal work versus unspecified "courses" and classroom years with no leadership role. That gap is what shifts a burden of proof in most equal-treatment frameworks.

So: lead with credentials, mention panel composition as context, not as your argument.

More urgent — your written request has gone unanswered. Many jurisdictions impose a response deadline on public appointments. Follow up in writing now, citing the relevant provision, and note the date of your original request.
